title: Basket, Umbrella, and Platform Trials: FDA Guidance Definitions and Design Expectations by Master-Protocol Type
summary: FDA definitions, design expectations, and regulatory requirements for basket, umbrella, and platform master-protocol trial types across key guidance documents.
body_markdown:
## Basket, umbrella, and platform trials: how FDA guidance defines and evaluates master-protocol designs


Master protocols have moved from a niche oncology tool to a mainstream development strategy, and FDA's written expectations have kept pace. The agency's thinking is spread across several documents: the oncology master-protocol guidance, the 2021 final COVID-19 master-protocol guidance, the animal-drug master-protocol guidance, and, most recently, a broad draft, *Master Protocols for Drug and Biological Product Development* (draft, issued June 24, 2026)[104](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=104) , which generalizes the concept beyond oncology[105](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=105) . This overview pulls the definitions and the design expectations that recur across those documents, organized by master-protocol type.


### What FDA means by "master protocol"


FDA defines a master protocol as a single protocol with multiple substudies designed to evaluate multiple hypotheses about one or more investigational products within an overall study structure[13](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=13) . The defining feature is shared infrastructure: one trial design and protocol that can evaluate multiple drugs, multiple diseases, or both[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=42) . Basket, umbrella, and platform designs are the three archetypes that sit under that umbrella term, differentiated by whether the multiplicity lies in the disease, in the drug, or in the time dimension.


Across guidance documents, the three types are defined as follows:


Design Core definition What varies


**Basket** Evaluates a single investigational drug (or combination) across multiple diseases, conditions, or disease subtypes[30](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=30)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=31) . The animal-drug guidance frames it as one drug in different populations defined by tumor type, stage, histology, prior therapy, or biomarker[13](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=13) . Multiple diseases/populations, one therapy


**Umbrella** Studies multiple products in parallel for a single disease or condition under one master protocol[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=32)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=31)[13](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=13) . Multiple therapies, one disease


**Platform** Evaluates multiple drugs for one or more diseases in an ongoing manner, with drugs entering or leaving the platform based on a prespecified decision algorithm[30](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=30)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=31) . Multiple therapies against a common control, evolving over time


The distinction matters because the statistical and operational risks differ by type: basket trials raise questions about pooling across heterogeneous populations, umbrella and platform trials raise questions about shared controls and multiplicity, and platform trials add the problem of comparisons drifting across calendar time.


### Basket trials


FDA treats basket trials as a collection of substudies, where each substudy carries its own objectives, design, conduct, and analysis for one drug in one disease, condition, or subtype[58](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=58) . The agency's expectations concentrate on how each substudy is specified and how results are interpreted across them.


- **Substudy architecture.** Basket-trial substudies are usually designed as single-arm, activity-estimating trials with overall response rate as the primary endpoint[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=91) . Each substudy should state specific objectives, the scientific rationale for including each population, and a detailed statistical analysis plan with sample-size justification and stopping rules for futility or efficacy[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=91) .
- **A clear primary objective for the whole trial.** Sponsors should specify and justify a clear primary objective for the overarching trial and explain how the design and analysis achieve it[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=81) .
- **Cohort expansion into a registrational path.** If a substudy shows a strong response signal, FDA notes the substudy may be expanded to generate data that could potentially support a marketing application[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=91) .
- **Interpretation: separate analysis is the default.** FDA describes two interpretation strategies: separate analyses confined to each substudy population, which is often most appropriate to minimize bias; or, where scientifically justified, leveraging information across related substudies qualitatively or quantitatively, including Bayesian borrowing[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=81) . If sponsors pool or borrow across substudies, they must justify the degree of relevance, including similarities in disease pathophysiology, how the drug is expected to modulate that pathophysiology (including pharmacokinetics), and endpoint/estimand attributes[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=81) .
- **Guarding against overinterpretation.** FDA warns that multiple study groups can lead to overinterpretation, including false apparent efficacy differences arising from multiple ad hoc between-arm comparisons[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=92) .
- **Submission structure.** For basket trials it may be appropriate to submit separate INDs for new substudies; sponsors should discuss the planned approach with the review division, weighing the populations, design, and whether analyses will leverage information across substudies[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=62) .


### Umbrella trials


Because an umbrella trial evaluates several therapies within one disease[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=31) , FDA's expectations center on preserving valid comparisons among those therapies.


- **Randomization where feasible.** FDA says comparisons among arms may be facilitated by randomization between the study arms, where feasible[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=32) , and that randomization ratios may be modified in adaptive designs, though this must be handled carefully[19](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=19) .
- **Shared control groups.** Umbrella trials may share a control group, which improves efficiency and simplifies study management[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=32) ; each drug is generally compared against a control arm[19](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=19) .
- **Eligibility-matched control.** To preserve valid comparisons, the control group for a given drug should generally include only participants who were concurrently eligible and could have been randomized to that drug[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=56) .


FDA's retrieved guidance is lighter on biomarker-stratification specifics for umbrella designs; the documents reference disease subtypes and eligibility criteria rather than prescribing a biomarker-stratification scheme[30](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=30)[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=56)[58](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=58)[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=34) .


### Platform trials


Platform trials are the most operationally complex master protocol: multiple therapies evaluated concurrently against a common control, running continuously as therapies enter and leave over time under prespecified rules[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=34)[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=87) .


- **Common control.** Platform (and umbrella) designs study multiple interventions concurrently against a common control group, with the comparison typically each individual drug versus that control arm[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=34)[19](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=19) .
- **Adding arms.** The design allows different drugs to enter the study at different times in a continuous manner[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=87) .
- **Dropping arms.** Drugs may leave the platform based on prespecified decision rules; more broadly, master protocols may use interim analyses to stop enrollment in a substudy for efficacy or futility[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=87)[19](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=19) .
- **Concurrent vs. nonconcurrent controls.** This is the design issue FDA emphasizes most for platform trials. Because a platform control arm can contain both participants enrolled concurrently with a given drug and participants randomized earlier (nonconcurrent controls who could not have been randomized to that drug)[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=56) , the primary comparison for a given drug should generally include only concurrently eligible controls and exclude nonconcurrent controls, as well as concurrently enrolled participants who could not have been randomized to that drug[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=56)[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=27) . FDA's rationale is that concurrently eligible controls preserve randomization and avoid bias from temporal changes in participant characteristics, trial conduct, or standard of care[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=27) . Nonconcurrent controls may be justified only in rare circumstances, with scientific justification addressing temporal shifts, the amount of nonconcurrent data, separation in calendar time, and statistical methods to mitigate bias; this should be discussed with FDA early and agreed before the trial starts[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=27) .


### Statistical design expectations across master-protocol types


FDA's statistical expectations apply across all three designs and are where many master protocols succeed or fail on review.


- **Type I error and multiplicity.** Master protocols should control type I error probability across the relevant multiple comparisons and control familywise type I error for each individual drug in its intended population across other multiplicity sources such as multiple endpoints[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=18) . Type I error control is especially important for closely related comparisons (multiple doses, administrations, or formulations of the same drug)[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=18) . For shared-control designs, the expected total number of type I errors may match separate trials, but the distribution of those errors differs, so sponsors should consider the probability of at least one error, the probability of multiple errors, power, and other operating characteristics[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=18) . In the COVID-19 umbrella/platform setting, FDA did not require multiplicity adjustment for multiple drug-versus-comparator comparisons to control overall familywise error, but still expected sponsors to weigh the possibility of multiple correlated erroneous findings rather than relying on a single p-value[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=22) .
- **Shared and common control arms.** Master protocols may use one common control arm or multiple control groups[13](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=13) , and sponsors may consider greater-than-equal allocation to control to reduce correlated erroneous findings and potentially improve power[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=18)[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=22) . When some participants are eligible only for some arms, the analysis for a given arm should compare against only the eligible control participants[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=22) .
- **Bayesian methods.** Bayesian methods may be used in adaptive and master-protocol settings, but the rationale should be clear and the conclusions sufficiently robust[12](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=12) . FDA notes Bayesian methods can inform adaptations while the primary analysis still uses a frequentist hypothesis test to control type I error[12](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=12) , and sponsors should justify that the prior, decision criteria, and adaptive elements achieve targeted operating characteristics (power, expected sample size, reliability of adaptation decisions) while maintaining type I error control[12](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=12) .
- **Adaptive features and interim analyses.** Master protocols may include interim analyses to stop enrollment for efficacy or futility, modify sample size, or modify the randomization ratio[19](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=19) . FDA's general adaptive-design principles apply: adaptations should be prespecified, supported by a detailed protocol and statistical analysis plan, and evaluated through simulation of operating characteristics including type I error, power, expected sample size, and bias[19](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=19)[17](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=17) . Interim analyses can also create confidentiality and interpretability issues when information from one substudy reveals information about another[19](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=19)[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=22) .


### Safety monitoring, oversight, and IND logistics


FDA's operational expectations reflect the fact that one master protocol may touch many drugs, sponsors, and sites at once.


- **Centralized safety reporting.** Safety reports from all clinical investigators flow to the master-protocol sponsor, who must report unexpected serious adverse events with a reasonable possibility of causation to FDA and all participating investigators, supported by a process for rapid communication of serious safety issues and rapid protocol amendment when needed[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=60)[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=61) .
- **Independent oversight.** FDA recommends a central IRB for the master protocol and an independent, external data monitoring committee (DMC) or comparable body to oversee accumulating safety and efficacy data[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=65)[57](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=57)[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=68) . The DMC charter should permit prespecified and ad hoc efficacy and futility reviews and recommendations for protocol modifications, including sample-size adjustment or stopping or modifying a substudy for futility or overwhelming efficacy[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=68) .
- **Protocol amendments.** Amendment cover letters should be labeled "Protocol Amendment-MASTER PROTOCOL"; substantive amendments affecting safety, quality, or scope should be submitted at least 30 days before changes begin, with the regulatory project manager notified at least 48 hours before submission[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=60)[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=61) . New investigational drugs or new substudies are added as amendments to the master-protocol IND[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=63)[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=64) .
- **IND structure.** Sponsors should request a pre-IND meeting early; master-protocol trials should generally be conducted under a single master-protocol IND, using Study Tagging Files and proper eCTD organization, and cross-referencing appropriately where separate substudy INDs are used[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=62)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=63)[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=64)[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=66) .


### Early engagement and the path to substantial evidence


FDA repeatedly stresses that master protocols are complex enough to warrant early and often iterative interaction. Sponsors should request a pre-IND meeting to discuss the protocol and submission logistics, and FDA notes multiple meetings may be needed; early engagement is particularly important when contemplating features such as nonconcurrent controls[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=62)[76](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=76)[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=27) . For rare-disease programs, innovative designs should be discussed in advance, ideally at the pre-IND meeting[78](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=78) .


On whether master-protocol data can support approval, FDA's position is conditional: master protocols may generate proof-of-concept, dose-ranging, effectiveness, and safety data, but whether a master protocol is adequate to contribute to a demonstration of substantial evidence of effectiveness depends on the design, conduct, and persuasiveness of the results[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=67)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=29) . Development programs often combine master protocols with stand-alone trials because different data types are needed, and the master protocol typically forms part of the overall safety database and benefit-risk assessment rather than the entire evidentiary basis[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=67)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=29)[74](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/basket-umbrella-and-platform-trials-how-fda?showSourceNumber=74) .
